title: RTL 2-die: SINGLE-packet cross-die deadlock at VCS=2 (table-routing build)

BookSim-exact Dijkstra tables route die-B west-of-bridge traffic through the phantom links -> at B(0,3) table port W = the bridge -> packet loops across the bridge forever (reproduced: 0->...->59->67->LOOP->59). onecell dst B(0,0) is west of the bridge. FIX (Dave's lane): remove the 2 anynet lines, regenerate tables (staged at /var/tmp/r1work/fixed_tables, 18/128 differ), rebuild, re-run onecell + F14. BookSim must use the fixed anynet for parity. This also re-frames 0344: the deadlock was this divergence, not VC capacity (d7fce0b's table approach was right; the tables inherited the phantom links).

title: gen_route_tables.py: anynet port numbering is file-order not geometric — bridge must be special-cased
description: BookSim anynet assigns ports by appearance order in the .anynet file (router 59's bridge link = outport 4), but RTL ports are geometric {E,W,N,S,L}. First version of gen_route_tables.py derived port geometrically -> router 59 gave die-B dsts port S instead of E, and die-B 67 gave W for die-A (correct by luck) but the reverse was wrong. Fixed in gen_route_tables.py: bridge directions forced E (die A) / W (die B) via bridge[] map. Lesson: any routing-table generator must map BookSim outports -> RTL geometry, not assume they align.

title: Cell authoring: empty trace files contaminate the sim (uninitialized BRAM garbage) — sentinel rule

The loccell/onecell cells all showed this. FIX: a no-traffic NIC must carry the sentinel line '0000000000000000' (cycle=0 → guard skips it), OR the file must not exist (fork-gate cells work with only trace_n0.hex present). Add to rtl_r1.py lint_cell (currently has uncommitted owner edits — add when clean): flag 0-byte trace files as a defect. Verified: sentinel traces change behavior (0 → 16,261 ejections, still garbage from partial files); only the sentinel/absent pattern is clean.
closeReason: FIXED (Steve, 2026-08-15): empty-trace lint added to rtl_r1.py (lint_trace_files, wired into gen_trace — an empty trace_n*.hex aborts gen-trace). Verified: empty files -> FAIL, sentinel (0000000000000000) / absent -> OK. The sentinel rule is now enforced, not just documented.
